Apple TV's new comedy "Brothers" has officially launched its first two episodes. The series stars Woody Harrelson (known for "Natural Born Killers") and Matthew McConaughey (known for "Interstellar"), and is now available for subscribers to stream. Check out the trailer below.

"Brothers" officially premieres on Apple TV

The two former co-stars of "True Detective" reunite on screen in Apple TV's new series "Brothers." The show draws inspiration from the long-standing rumor that Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson are actually half-brothers.

"Brothers" was announced last June, with Lee Eisenberg (known for his work on "The Office" and "Jury Duty") serving as showrunner. In addition to starring in the series, both leads also serve as executive producers.

This marks Matthew McConaughey's second collaboration with Apple TV, following last year's Apple original film "The Lost Bus"; Woody Harrelson is likewise appearing on the platform for the second time, having played Moe Berkus in "Fly Me to the Moon."

"Brothers" will run for eight episodes this season, with new episodes releasing every Wednesday through November 4.
